facts.raw_span: recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol
symptoms persisting for 2 years but worsening on admission
symptoms usually occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion and lasted 5-10 minutes
syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
hypertension diagnosed 3 months prior
smoking and alcohol overconsumption (250g/week) for about 20 years
No specific physical examination findings were documented in the case report
High-sensitivity troponin I: 0.01 ng/mL (normal)
Serum potassium: 4.6 mEq/L (normal)
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol, combined with ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions, suggest alcoholic cardiomyopathy.
The patient's history of hypertension and ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions may indicate hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
The patient's coronary angiography results showing 10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA) suggest coronary artery disease.
The patient's history of alcohol overconsumption and hypertension diagnosis suggest alcohol-induced hypertension.
The patient's symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain after drinking alcohol may indicate gastroesophageal reflux disease.
The patient's history of alcohol overconsumption and symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain suggest alcoholic gastritis.

rationales.F01: Recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol suggests a relationship between alcohol consumption and symptoms, which is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and other alcohol-related conditions.
rationales.F03: The timing of symptoms in relation to alcohol ingestion is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and other alcohol-related conditions.
rationales.F04: Syncope occurring only after large alcohol intake suggests a dose-dependent relationship, which is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and other alcohol-related conditions.
rationales.F05: Hypertension is a known risk factor for various cardiovascular conditions, including Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy, but in this context, it more strongly supports Alcohol-Induced Hypertension.
rationales.F06: Long-term smoking and alcohol overconsumption are risk factors for multiple conditions, including Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy, Coronary Artery Disease, and alcohol-related gastrointestinal disorders.
rationales.F10: High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions are indicative of cardiac dysfunction, which is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F11: ST segment elevations and depressions are indicative of myocardial ischemia or infarction, which can be seen in Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and Coronary Artery Disease.
rationales.F12: Mild stenosis in the coronary arteries is less indicative of significant Coronary Artery Disease but does not rule out Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy or other cardiac conditions.
